title: Points and graphs you will actually use
hook: A pump's curve shows the head it gives at each flow, and more flow means less head. How do you read the head for the flow you need straight off the graph?
oneBreath: A point on a grid is named by two numbers, (x, y): how far along from (0, 0), then how far up, always in that order. Negative numbers send you left or down, so the grid has four quarters, and a zero puts the point on an axis. A square on a graph need not be worth 1, so read the scale from the axis labels and keep its steps equal. Plot a table of measurements as points, then draw one best straight line or smooth curve through them rather than joining the dots. Read a graph both ways, up from a flow to a pump's curve and across to its head, or back again, and trust a reading inside the measured points more than one beyond them. When two things are in proportion their graph is a straight line through (0, 0), like a resistor's voltage against its current from V = IR, and with voltage up the side a steeper line means more ohms.

ideas.title: Along, then up
ideas.oneLine: (3, 2) means 3 along then 2 up from (0, 0), x before y, so swapping the numbers puts the point somewhere else.

ideas.title: All four quadrants
ideas.oneLine: Negatives go left or down, so the signs of (x, y) name the quarter and a zero puts the point on an axis.

ideas.title: Scales
ideas.oneLine: A square need not be 1: read the axis labels, read between the marks, and choose equal steps of 1, 2 or 5 so the data fits.

ideas.title: From a table to a graph
ideas.oneLine: Plot each row of a table as a point, then draw one best straight line or smooth curve through measured points instead of joining the dots.

ideas.title: Reading a graph
ideas.oneLine: Read up from a flow to a pump's curve and across to its head, or back, and trust readings inside the data, not beyond.

ideas.title: Straight lines through zero
ideas.oneLine: Two things in proportion make a straight line through (0, 0), like a resistor's V-I graph from V = IR; a bend or a miss means not proportional.

calibration.q: Which point is 2 along and 5 up from (0, 0)?
calibration.why: The first number says how far along and the second how far up, so it is (2, 5). (5, 2) swaps them, which lands 5 along and 2 up, and (7, 0) adds them together.

calibration.q: A resistor passes 2 A at 10 V. On its graph, with current along the bottom and voltage up the side, which point is at 4 A?
calibration.why: Its graph is a straight line through zero, so double the current gives double the voltage: 4 A at 20 V. (4, 12) adds 2 to each number, and (4, 10) keeps the voltage the same.
